body: The "[configure a fallback route on your server](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/19009#issuecomment-326727616)" solution proposed by @Toxicable, and the [Apache deployment solution](https://github.com/mgechev/angular-seed/wiki/Deploying-prod-build-to-Apache-2) both suggest either add server routes or use hashLocationStrategy.

Arguably, the documentation is correct there because it's talking about router navigations, which _are_ strictly a local url and do not result in a server request. A direct url navigation or hard page refresh is a navigation triggered by the browser rather than the Angular router. But I agree that there could be some clarification in the docs there.

When the app is hosted on a Web server with no error rewrite rules and I navigate to
/basehref/index.html OK
But
When I go 'deep' I get server generated 404.

From that experience I was wondering if the change in URL actually does get validated at the server.

Thank you for the link. It says: "The browser makes a direct request to the server for that URL, bypassing the router." just reinforces the misleading statement of "as this is a strictly local URL the browser won't send this URL to the server" on  https://angular.io/guide/router#locationstrategy-and-browser-url-styles

@OzBob - Again, the statement you’re pointing to is referring to navigations through the Angular router. Deep links go to the server because there’s no page loaded. My opinion is that it’s not misleading at all but could potentially use clarification.
